messages:
Diego Ruiz: Quick heads-up: leadership wants clearer acceptance criteria for the attention micro-optimizations RFC. I floated a set in PRD but want runtime folks to sanity check.
Nora Kim: paste it here plz.
Diego Ruiz: Extract: 
```
ATTN MICRO-OPTIMIZATIONS - ACCEPTANCE SUMMARY:
- Implementation must be feature-flagged and off by default on Hosted.
- End-to-end latency improvement >= 7% on P50 and >= 5% on P95 for transformer-decoder models on seq lengths 32/256/1024.
- No regression in generation quality: BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy metrics delta < 0.8% vs baseline.
- Existing eval suites must pass with quantized kernels.
- Fallback semantics: if attention op fails (e.g., OOM or kernel crash) we must fall back to a robust attention kernel with <2x perf cost.
```
Samir Das: Are the perf numbers realistic for 1024? caches + kernel changes often give big wins on 32/256 but marginal on 1024. We should call out that 1024 is best-effort.
Anya Volkova: Also add that for Dedicated we can enable earlier with a dedicated perf SLA and customer opt-in.
InfraBot: perf-test: queued job id=perf-2362400001, suite=attn-microopt, targets=[32,256,1024]
Diego Ruiz: Good notes. I'll mark 1024 as "best-effort" and require at least no P95 regression for that bucket.
Nora Kim: Add observability hooks: expose attention_kernel.version and per-request attention_fallback.reason.
Samir Das: Edge-case: fused attention may not support past-state caching for incremental decode; ensure we test prefix cache correctness.
Diego Ruiz: Add prefix cache correctness test and quality regression harness.
Anya Volkova: We should also include a fallback timeline: if we detect >1% error rate in canary for 30m, auto-disable the micro-opt for that cluster.
Diego Ruiz: Ok set auto-disable to 30m/1% for hosted, and allow 10m/3% for Dedicated with customer opt-in.
Nora Kim: I'm +1 to feature-flag and off-by-default.
Diego Ruiz: Action items: Diego to update RFC, Samir to draft prefix-cache tests, Anya to update rollout policy. RFC review Fri 3pm.
